08 FOR EDUCATORS & TRAINERS

Film a course your learners can follow.

When a learner pauses your video to try the next step, what needs to be in the frame? Bring one lesson to work through. We can put the presenter on one camera and the detail on another.

Plan course filming ↗Session rates ↗

01 SESSION NOTES

Plan the shoot around the lesson.

01

Start with a pilot lesson

List what the learner should be able to do afterwards. Bring your slides or props and mark the points where a close-up or a screen recording would help.

02

Batch the repeatable parts

Film the introductions while the desk is set, then move to the bench for the demonstrations. A reference photo helps us match the framing if you add a module later.

03

Decide what the learner receives

A single lecture and eight individually titled lessons need different edits. Include chapter names, caption languages and your learning platform’s file requirements in the brief.

02 BEFORE YOU RECORD

Good questions.

Can we film an internal training course?

Yes. Bring the person who knows the process and a sample of the materials they use. Tell us which steps can appear on screen and which need dummy data.

How is a course shoot priced?

We quote by recording time, setup changes and the number of finished modules. A short pilot gives us a basis for costing the rest of the course.

Put your session on paper.

Choose a starting point and save a brief. Pilot prices and dates are confirmed separately.
